descriptions.title: Windows orchestrates, WSL2 does the heavy lifting
descriptions.body: The studio is a Windows Python process, but every GPU-heavy step runs inside WSL2 Ubuntu-24.04. avatar_studio.py shells out with `wsl -d Ubuntu-24.04 bash -c '<cmd>'` for LivePortrait, Hallo2, video-retalking, and all ffmpeg/ffprobe work. Each render model lives in its own conda env (liveportrait, hallo, retalking) so their conflicting CUDA/dlib/numpy requirements never collide. to_wsl_path() rewrites C:\... to /mnt/c/... (and quotes paths with spaces) for every file handed across the boundary. This split is why the install fixes in CLAUDE.md (dlib CPU-only, GPEN CUDA symlinks, numpy-2.x basicsr patches) all live on the WSL2 side, not in the Windows venv.

descriptions.title: Two TTS engines, routed per language
descriptions.body: Voice generation is dual-engine and the choice is data-driven from languages.json, not hardcoded. Kokoro-82M (local, offline, Apache 2.0) serves the six languages it has good voices for — American & British English, Brazilian Portuguese, Spanish, Italian, Mandarin. The other four — Japanese, French, Russian, German — route to Microsoft Edge Neural voices via edge-tts because Kokoro-82M lacks them (no male French voice; Windows pyopenjtalk broken for Japanese). generate_voice() reads the engine field and either runs an async edge_tts.Communicate (rate/pitch as SSML) or a Kokoro KPipeline (chunks concatenated, written at 24 kHz, pitch optionally shifted by SciPy resampling).

descriptions.title: Swappable render engines behind one pipeline
descriptions.body: pipeline_generate() is engine-agnostic: it produces the WAV, prepares the portrait, then dispatches to whichever engine the UI selected — run_liveportrait, run_hallo2, run_heygen, run_did, run_musetalk, run_sadtalker, or run_wav2lip — and optionally runs run_retalking afterward. get_engine_choices() decides which engines are even offered: LivePortrait and Hallo2 are always available; cloud engines appear only when both an api_key and the enabled flag are present; the extra WSL2 engines appear only when enabled in studio_config.json. Adding an engine is one run_* function plus a branch in the dispatch ladder.

descriptions.title: LivePortrait vs Hallo2 — speed vs lip accuracy
descriptions.body: The two local engines make opposite trade-offs. LivePortrait transfers motion from a curated driving video (d13 recommended) and renders in ~30 seconds, but the mouth follows the driving clip, not the script — so lips don't match the audio unless the optional video-retalking pass is enabled. Hallo2 is fully audio-driven: the mouth is generated from the WAV itself, so lip sync is native, at the cost of ~15-30 minutes per minute of audio. run_hallo2 also re-muxes our exact WAV over Hallo2's output with ffmpeg (-map 0:v:0 -map 1:a:0) so the rendered script is guaranteed to be what's heard. Lip sync is the project's #1 open issue.

descriptions.title: Secrets kept out of the repo
descriptions.body: Cloud API keys never live in version-controlled config. studio_config.json holds only the enabled flags and (blank) key slots; the real keys come from secrets/avatarstudio.env (gitignored) or environment variables, mapped by _SECRET_MAP (did -> DID_API_KEY, heygen -> HEYGEN_API_KEY). _apply_secret_overlay() injects them into the in-memory config at load time, and save_studio_config() deep-copies and blanks every key before writing the file back — so a key can never be accidentally persisted. The git baseline commit's message records exactly this hardening: 'secrets moved out of studio_config.json'.

descriptions.title: Scene pipeline — one script to a multi-character movie
descriptions.body: scene_pipeline.py extends the single-clip studio into a movie maker. A full script is split into scenes three ways: manual (--- breaks with optional [Name] or [Name:photo] tags), AI (NEXUS LLM split for intelligent scene boundaries), or hybrid (LLM split then user-editable before render). Characters are decoupled from agents.json — any photo and name via characters.json or inline syntax — with the agent roster offered only as a convenience. run_pipeline() renders each scene through the same TTS->render->retalking path, then concat_scenes() stitches the per-scene MP4s into one final movie with ffmpeg. The AI split depends on NEXUS being reachable; it falls back to a rule-based splitter otherwise.
